name: Budget Guardian
description: Personal finance desktop application built as a data structures and algorithms showcase. Every core feature is intentionally implemented on custom, from-scratch data structures rather than the Java Collections Framework.

techStack.persistence: Pluggable: SQLite via JDBC (local mode) or REST backend (api mode)
techStack.documentation: Javadoc on all public types and methods
techStack.backend: Node.js + Express 5 + Prisma ORM -> Neon PostgreSQL (backend/)

coreConstraint.rule: No java.util Collections (ArrayList, LinkedList, HashMap, HashSet, PriorityQueue, Stack, Queue, etc.) may be used as storage or in business logic.
allowedExceptions: JDBC ResultSet iteration inside repository classes (unavoidable interop)
JavaFX ObservableList at the UI rendering boundary only, populated by copying from a custom structure immediately before display, never used as a data store
java.util.NoSuchElementException / ConcurrentModificationException as thrown exception types (not storage)
coreConstraint.enforcement: ArchitectureGuardTest scans src/main/java under datastructures, model, repository, service, and algorithm packages and fails the build if a forbidden java.util collection import is found.

layering: Storage (persistence only, never queried at runtime after startup): SQLite file OR REST backend -> Prisma -> Neon PostgreSQL
Repository interfaces (repository/) with two implementations: repository/sqlite (JDBC) and repository/api (HTTP+JSON)
Service layer (business logic, validation, undo, rules, notifications, reports)
JavaFX UI (views + dialogs, subscribed to EventBus)
architecture.dataFlowDirection: Storage -> Repository -> DataStore (custom structures) -> Service -> UI. UI never accesses storage or HTTP directly; the desktop never connects to PostgreSQL and holds no database credentials.
writePathSteps: Persist via repository interfaces (TransactionRunner) - storage-first ordering; one SQLite transaction locally, atomic REST endpoints in api mode
Push the inverse Action onto the undo Stack
Re-run the RuleEngine (danger spending, daily budget, debt overdue, refill overdue)
Publish an EventType on the EventBus so subscribed views refresh
architecture.compositionRoot: com.budgetguardian.service.ServiceContext wires repositories, DataStore (via StartupLoader), every service, NotificationService, and RuleEngine into one object graph. com.budgetguardian.app.Main constructs it and builds the JavaFX shell on top.

storageModes.configFile: config.properties in the per-user data directory (seeded from an annotated bundled template on first launch)
storageModes.local: SQLite file in the user data directory (default, offline)
storageModes.api: REST backend selected by api.baseUrl; optional X-API-Key; timeouts and idempotent-only retries configurable

cloudPersistence.chain: Java Desktop -> Repository layer -> HTTP REST API -> Node.js (Express) -> Prisma -> Neon PostgreSQL

designPatterns.description: One repository class per aggregate; JDBC-only, never returns java.util collections.
All business rules, validation and orchestration.
view classes act as both controller and view; model holds immutable domain records.
Publish/subscribe; services publish EventType values, views subscribe. Zero direct coupling.
Every mutation is an undoable command carrying enough state (a memento snapshot) to invert itself.
Sort/search algorithm is injected, not hardcoded.

customDataStructures.name: DynamicArray<T>
customDataStructures.resizePolicy: doubles capacity when full; halves when size drops to 1/4 capacity, never below default (8)

customDataStructures.name: DoublyLinkedList<T>
customDataStructures.backing: doubly linked nodes with head/tail references

customDataStructures.name: HashMap<K,V>
customDataStructures.backing: separate-chaining hash table, 16 initial buckets, 0.75 load factor, bit-spread hash (h ^ (h >>> 16))

customDataStructures.name: Stack<T>
usedFor: undo action history (session-only, unbounded, no redo)

customDataStructures.name: Queue<T>
customDataStructures.backing: singly linked nodes with head+tail references

customDataStructures.name: PriorityQueue<T>
customDataStructures.backing: binary max-heap stored inside a DynamicArray
usedFor: hero alert banner: only the single highest-priority notification is shown

customDataStructures.name: CircularBuffer<T>
customDataStructures.backing: fixed-size ring array with head index and size counter

customDataStructures.name: Graph<T>
customDataStructures.backing: HashMap<T, DoublyLinkedList<Edge<T>>> adjacency list, directed weighted multigraph

complexity.dfs: O(V+E), iterative using an explicit Stack

customAlgorithms.name: MergeSort
customAlgorithms.notes: Available strategy implementation; demonstrates stable ordering.

customAlgorithms.name: QuickSort
customAlgorithms.complexity: O(n log n) average, O(n^2) worst
customAlgorithms.notes: Median-of-three pivot selection to reduce worst-case likelihood.

customAlgorithms.name: HeapSort
customAlgorithms.notes: Used by ReportService to rank categories by spend.

customAlgorithms.name: LinearSearch
customAlgorithms.notes: Used by SearchService for free-text ledger search.

money.rationale: exact arithmetic, no floating-point rounding drift

debt.autoSettle: a debt transitions to SETTLED once the sum of its payments reaches the full amount

refillItems.detection: duplicate purchase of the same normalized item name triggers a 'keep as refillable?' prompt
refillItems.persistence: only a 'Yes' answer is stored permanently; 'No' stores nothing so the prompt re-appears on the next duplicate
refillItems.interval: running average of days between purchases, recalculated on every confirmed purchase

transfers.rule: transfers are never expenses or income; they only move balance between two accounts and are tracked in a dedicated model, table, service and graph edge

debtOverdue.condition: an OPEN debt has a dueDate strictly before today

dailyReminder.condition: no EXPENSE transaction recorded for today, checked once per calendar day by a 60-second-tick daemon scheduler

undo.scope: every mutating operation (add/edit/delete transaction, transfer, debt payment, refill confirmation)
undo.persistence: session-only; the undo stack is not saved to the database and is empty after every application restart

database.accessPattern: hydrated fully into memory once at startup by StartupLoader; never queried again until the next application start

categories: service (business logic, undo round-trips, rule engine, reminders)
architecture guard (fails build on forbidden java.util collection imports)
integration sync (full service layer over REST repositories: hydration, remote-first writes, undo restore, failure keeps memory intact, restart consistency)

fatJar.reason: Launcher does not extend javafx.application.Application directly, avoiding the 'JavaFX runtime components are missing' error when JavaFX is on the classpath instead of the module path.
